claims: The Jones Act is the Merchant Marine Act of 1920.
The Jones Act is a U.S. federal statute.
The Jones Act requires that all goods transported by water between U.S. ports be carried on U.S.-built ships.
The Jones Act requires that all goods transported by water between U.S. ports be carried on U.S.-owned ships.
The Jones Act requires that all goods transported by water between U.S. ports be carried on U.S.-flagged ships.
The Jones Act requires that all goods transported by water between U.S. ports be carried on U.S.-crewed ships.
The Jones Act was enacted post-WWI.
The Jones Act was designed to ensure a strong merchant marine for national defense.
The Jones Act was designed to maintain a shipbuilding industry.
Under the Jones Act, a ship must be registered in the U.S.
Under the Jones Act, a ship must be owned by U.S. citizens.
Under the Jones Act, a ship must be built in the U.S.
Under the Jones Act, a ship must be crewed by Americans.
The Jones Act forbids foreign-flagged vessels from transporting goods directly between two U.S. points.
The Jones Act forbids foreign-built vessels from transporting goods directly between two U.S. points.
The Jones Act applies to all U.S. coastal waters.
The Jones Act applies to all U.S. inland waterways.
The Jones Act applies to shipping to and from Alaska.
The Jones Act applies to shipping to and from Hawaii.
The Jones Act applies to shipping to and from Puerto Rico.
The Jones Act allows U.S. seamen injured in the course of their work to bring negligence claims against their employers.
The Jones Act allows U.S. seamen the right to a jury trial.
The Secretary of Defense can waive Jones Act requirements for national defense reasons.
The Secretary of Homeland Security can waive Jones Act requirements for national defense reasons.
Proponents argue that the Jones Act is essential to maintaining a reliable maritime fleet for emergency use.
Critics contend that the Jones Act increases the cost of shipping goods between U.S. ports.
Critics contend that the Jones Act significantly impacts the cost of goods for non-continental U.S. territories like Puerto Rico and Alaska.
The Jones Act supports domestic shipyards.
The Jones Act keeps American mariners employed.
